Any octave counts
Sing in whatever octave fits your voice
Tips: If notes feel too high or low, drag Key transpose until the bubbles sit comfortably in your range. If your voice line looks late/early compared to when you actually sing, adjust Mic timing offset. Slow the Tempo down while learning, then bring it back up.

Your vocal range

A2 – A4
Every exercise is built to fit between your lowest and highest note.
Sing your LOWEST comfortable note on "oooh" and hold it…
–

5-Note Scale Ladder

Do-re-mi-fa-sol and back down. Climbs a half-step each rep through your whole range. The classic daily warmup.

Full Major Scale

Up and down the full octave scale. Great for evenness between notes once you're warm.

Arpeggio 1-3-5-8

Skipping between chord tones — trains accuracy on jumps, not just steps.

Octave Leaps

Low note, jump the octave, land back down. Builds range and confidence at the top.

Note Match

You hear a note — sing it back and hold it. 10 rounds.

Keyboard

A playable keyboard. Press a note, hear it, sing it back — and watch exactly where you landed. Note Match, except you pick the note.

Sustain Hold

Hold one note dead steady for 5 seconds. Trains breath support and stops the wobble.

Warmup syllable

Sung on every ladder note. "Mee" for brightness, "Noo/Loo" for smoothness.

Karaoke

Almost every song has a karaoke / instrumental version on YouTube already. Find it, paste the link, and sing over it while the app tracks your pitch live. Wired headphones in — so the mic only hears you.
Song key Pick the key. The notes in that key light up as you sing.
–
sing to see your note
–
Steady
Steady is how still you held the pitch over the last second. 100% is dead still; anything above about 85% is a held note rather than a wobble. It only moves while you are singing.
Tip: add the word "karaoke" or "instrumental with lyrics" to get versions with no lead vocal and on-screen words. The blue line is your voice — keep it flat and on a note line.
